source_review.notes: Checked the primary GFS and Ceph papers, standards-track NFSv4 specification, and current official HDFS and CephFS architecture, HA, federation, locking, multi-MDS, and cache documentation. Sources support namespace/data separation, stable file identity, journal/checkpoint recovery, active/standby fencing, independent federation, dynamic subtree ownership, client capabilities, referrals, and atomic-operation claims. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed versioned namespace tuple, dentry key/value types, generation-qualified identities, path-resolution function, transaction tuple, log sequences, checkpoints, routing maps, and memory-accounting variables.
Checked integer sequence intervals, strict transaction preconditions, ceiling division, occupancy bounds, and the distinction between namespace version, routing epoch, and inode generation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Names, stable identities, versions, commit positions, ownership epochs, and physical data locations remain distinct throughout.

evidence: Executed namespace-transaction-accounting with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced the four output lines for pre/post rename state, commit sequence, stale conflict, snapshot state, and capacity.

Recomputed 13 million inodes at 320 bytes, 13 million dentries at 160 bytes, 72 million block references at 32 bytes, and 600 MiB runtime state as 9,173,145,600 bytes and 12,230,860,800 bytes at 75 percent occupancy.
Recomputed exercise two as 6,000 entries and 0.08 seconds ideal replay, and exercise four as 18,110,612,736 bytes and 25,872,303,909 installed bytes at 70 percent occupancy.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Capacity examples identify binary GiB/MiB, round installed bytes upward, and explicitly exclude implementation and failover overheads.

evidence: Expanded component-wise path resolution as repeated dentry mapping from a named root under one namespace version and credential context.
Checked recovery equivalence by applying the contiguous committed journal suffix after checkpoint position k and excluding duplicate, missing, or uncommitted records.
Derived resident state as the sum of count-times-measured-size classes plus runtime state and installed capacity as the ceiling of resident state divided by target occupancy.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formulas are conditional models and do not imply a universal metadata representation, consistency model, or capacity constant.

evidence: Reviewed empty/root/relative paths, dot components, links, mounts, Unicode and case normalization, loops, depth limits, stale handles, concurrent ancestor changes, replacement rename, open-unlinked files, and snapshot roots.

Reviewed duplicate retry, partial journal tail, sequence gap, corrupt checkpoint, lagging standby/follower, paused old leader, stale route, migration cutover, cross-shard rename, capability-revocation loss, hot directory, and checkpoint/replay pressure.
Reviewed permission changes, tenant-handle crossover, sensitive names in metrics, audit retention, legal holds, key loss, archival state, and application-inconsistent snapshots.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter distinguishes normal not-found or stale-handle outcomes from structural corruption, ambiguous commit, unavailable authority, and policy denial.

evidence: Traced dentry-to-inode identity, directory-cycle and link state, transaction atomicity, durable sequence order, checkpoint/log compatibility, one writable authority per epoch, and cache validity through exposition and examples.
Checked that cross-shard and cross-volume boundaries do not silently weaken promised rename semantics and that old authorities and client tokens are fenced.
Checked that open handles, snapshots, clones, holds, and grace periods remain garbage-collection roots after unlink.
invariant_checking.notes: Routing, caching, persistence, snapshotting, and data placement cannot independently authorize a namespace mutation.

evidence: Reviewed all ten metadata-service audit obligations from naming and traversal through transactions, recovery, fencing, routing, resources, and adversarial testing.

Checked counterexamples for path-equals-identity, directory-equals-map, rename-equals-copy/delete, log-file-equals-durable, checkpoint-equals-backup, election-equals-fencing, TTL-equals-coherence, process-count-equals-throughput, hash-equals-balanced, and unlink-equals-deletable claims.
Reviewed atomic rename, checkpoint-plus-log recovery, one-authority fencing, cache revocation, migration cutover, and reclamation proof boundaries.
proof_review.notes: Safety, durability, availability, cache coherence, scalability, security, retention, and application consistency are separate evidence obligations.

evidence: Audited uses of atomic, consistent, authoritative, current, durable, safe, exact, complete, correct, proof, and equivalence.
Confirmed the executable fixture is labeled as an in-memory reasoning aid rather than a persistent filesystem, distributed transaction protocol, authorization proof, or production benchmark.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: System-specific semantics are attributed to primary or current official sources and general claims state their preconditions.

evidence: Reviewed retrieval dates, operation distributions, hot-directory rates, object-size distributions, lock and journal metrics, checkpoint age, replay rate, standby lag, cache state, routing redirects, failure injection, and restore trials.
Confirmed no production scale, universal POSIX compliance, recovery objective, legal approval, research-governance approval, certification, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production claims require exact implementation/version, workloads, state size, cache state, fault model, persistence topology, security controls, and repeated recovery evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed names and stable identities, path resolution, dentries/inodes, namespace transactions, journal/checkpoint recovery, HA fencing, leases/capabilities, snapshots, sharding, routing, cross-shard operations, hotspots, capacity, security, and observability as one coherent model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed idempotent mutation APIs, journal durability, checkpoint manifests, standby lag, fencing sinks, client cache revocation, directory fragmentation, ownership migration, cross-volume behavior, memory/replay sizing, sensitive telemetry, and restore drills. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from names and identity through transactions, persistence, availability, caching, snapshots, scaling, operations, and governance; ten examples and five complete answers cover rename, recovery, federation/sharding, capacity, and archival migration.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external filesystem researcher, metadata-service operator, storage vendor, security auditor, records authority, research-governance body, archive custodian, or certification review is claimed.
